methods.label: Choose the adjacent letter positions
methods.explanation:
First choose where the adjacent letters go. Their first position can be 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5, giving five possible placements.

For each placement, choose each of the four digits in 10 ways and each of the two letters in 26 ways. Repetition is allowed, and zero is allowed in any digit position because these are license plate codes. The multiplication principle gives
\[
5\cdot10^4\cdot26^2.
\]
Every valid plate has a unique first letter position and a unique ordered choice of its characters, so every plate is counted exactly once. The answer is \(\boxed{5\cdot10^4\cdot26^2}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
